# Your Hospital Discharge Letter

**For: Mavis**
**Date of discharge: To be confirmed**

Dear Mavis,

This letter tells you what happened during your stay in hospital, what was done to help you, and what happens next. Please keep it somewhere safe and share it with your GP.

---

## Why you came into hospital

You came in after a fall at home. Your son found you on the floor. You were checked over carefully when you arrived.

During your stay you became more unwell. The team found that you had:

- **A chest infection (possible aspiration pneumonia)** — an infection in the lower part of your right lung.
- **An inflamed bowel (sigmoid diverticulitis)** — a part of your large bowel became inflamed.
- **A serious infection in your body (sepsis)** — your body was fighting a significant infection.
- **A short-term drop in how well your kidneys were working (acute kidney injury)** — this improved during your stay.
- **A brief abnormal heart rhythm (atrial flutter)** — this was picked up on a heart tracing when you arrived.

You also have a number of longer-term health conditions that the team were aware of throughout your care.

---

## What was done to help you

When you arrived, the team did scans of your head, neck, and chest to make sure you had not been seriously hurt in the fall. These scans did not show any new injuries.

When you became more unwell in early May, the team acted quickly. You were given:

- **A strong antibiotic drip (piperacillin-tazobactam / Tazocin)** to treat the infection.
- **A drip of fluids** to support your body.
- **Extra oxygen** to help your breathing.
- **Medicine to stop you feeling sick (antiemetics)** — the exact medicine used was not recorded in the notes.

The team kept a very close eye on you. Your son Steven was kept informed throughout, including during the most difficult part of your illness.

You got better. By the time you were ready to go home, you were awake and aware, you had stopped being sick, and your tummy was comfortable.

---

## Your medicines

> ⚠ **This section cannot be completed yet.**

What we do know is that before you came in, you were taking **two blood-thinning medicines (dual antiplatelet therapy)** after your recent heart event. Whether you should continue these, and whether any new medicines have been added or any stopped, needs to be confirmed by your doctor before you go home.

---

## What happens next

Several things still need to be arranged or confirmed by your care team. These include:

- **A memory clinic appointment** — the team noted that a referral to a memory clinic was recommended. Whether this has been sent needs to be checked.
- **Follow-up for your inflamed bowel (diverticulitis)** — no outpatient appointment has been arranged yet; this needs to be confirmed.
- **Your heart rhythm (atrial flutter)** — the team need to confirm whether any further checks or treatment are needed for this.
- **Your kidneys** — your kidneys were affected during this admission. Whether you need blood tests to check on them after you go home needs to be confirmed.

Your GP will also receive a copy of your discharge summary and should be aware of your recent admission.

---

## If you are worried

The team did not document specific warning signs to watch for at home. Please use the general advice below:

If you become unwell or are worried about anything, contact your GP or call NHS 111. Call 999 if it is an emergency.
